text.p: Deutsche Telekom's stock offering, the biggest ever in Europe, was still oversubscribed after the giant German phone company increased the number of shares by 20 percent, banking sources said Tuesday.

The initial public offering, to begin next week when shares start trading in Germany, New York and Tokyo, was increased Monday by 100 million shares to 690 million shares. That raised the offering's potential value to as much as 18 billion marks ($12 billion) from 15 billion ($9.9 billion).
The sources said that despite the increase in the number of shares, the offer was still oversubscribed by four times.
The company said Tuesday that nearly 1.5 million German private investors had placed firm orders to buy at least 100 shares in Deutsche Telekom when it goes public next Monday.
About 70 percent of the shares will be placed in Germany, divided between individual and institutional investors.
